explicit_propositions.text: Climate change is real and human-caused.
The speaker believes climate change represents a 'silent and slow-moving Sputnik moment'.
Free enterprise can solve challenges like climate change.
The speaker supports the precautionary principle and data-driven analysis.
The speaker rejects the alt-right and opposes their influence on the Republican Party.
The speaker believes in protecting life of the unborn.
The speaker believes the government should not regulate private consensual adult relationships.
The speaker fears populist nationalism and views it as destructive to democratic institutions.
The speaker believes that nostalgia for past eras like the 1950s and 1960s is based on false memories of progress.
The speaker urges members of Congress to lead boldly despite political risks.

assumptions.text: A conservative member of Congress has a moral obligation to lead with courage and vision.
True conservatism values innovation, economic prosperity, and national unity over reactionary nostalgia.
Public leadership requires personal sacrifice and willingness to face electoral consequences.
American exceptionalism is rooted in technological ambition, optimism, and collective action.
Audience members identify with the described idealized conservative figure and will respond emotionally to appeals to shared ideals.
The public desires unifying narratives and can be rallied around pragmatic solutions to existential challenges.
Historical progress is possible through sustained commitment to science, free markets, and institutional stability.
Conservatives can authentically embrace environmental responsibility without abandoning core ideological principles.
Political courage is more valuable than popularity or conformity within one’s party.
The speaker’s vision of conservatism reflects a broader, legitimate strand within the Republican Party that deserves recognition and amplification.
